name: MonarchEmojiPicker
title: EmojiPicker
summary: An emoji picker with category tabs, recently used emoji first and skin-tone variants: the AndroidX system EmojiPickerView, hosted in Compose.
whenToUse: To let people choose any emoji for a reaction or a message, usually in a MonarchBottomSheet opened from a reaction or emoji button, or as the picker of MonarchReactionBar.
whenNotToUse: For a few fixed reactions use a row of buttons or MonarchReactionBar quickReactions. For typing emoji in text, the keyboard already has a picker with search.
api: @Composable public fun MonarchEmojiPicker(onEmojiPicked: (String) -> Unit, modifier: Modifier = Modifier, columns: Int? = null, rows: Float? = null, label: String? = null)

options.name: onEmojiPicked
options.description: Called with the emoji the person picks, including the skin-tone variant chosen with a long press.

options.name: modifier
options.description: The modifier of the picker. It fills the width and is 320dp high unless the modifier sets a size first.

options.name: columns
options.description: Emoji per row. null keeps the view's 9.

options.name: rows
options.description: Rows visible at once; a fraction shows that the grid scrolls. null keeps the view's 7.5.

options.name: label
options.description: The pane name TalkBack reads; the built-in "Emoji" (monarch_emojipicker_label) without it.

states.name: default
states.description: Category tabs over a scrolling grid; the first tab holds the recently used emoji once the person has picked one.

states.name: variant menu
states.description: A long press on an emoji with skin-tone or gender variants opens the view's own popup of variants.

appearance: EmojiPickerView draws its own tabs and grid and takes its colors from the Activity's View theme, not from MonarchTheme; place it on a raised surface such as a MonarchBottomSheet. Light, dark and high-contrast themes are not checked on a device yet.
platformNotes: The web EmojiPicker and the iOS MonarchEmojiPicker are custom pickers with a bundled index of 517 emoji, search, categories, recents and skin tones, because neither platform has a picker outside the keyboard. Android has one in AndroidX, so Monarch hosts EmojiPickerView instead of drawing one: it covers recents, skin-tone and gender variants and the emoji font of the device. It has no search field and no categories or recents parameters; the keyboard's emoji search covers search. Recently used emoji are kept by the view in the app's shared preferences.
accessibility: The picker is a pane named "Emoji" (or label) and a traversal group, so TalkBack announces it when it appears in a sheet.
Each emoji in the grid and each category tab is read by the AndroidX view itself; this is not covered by Robolectric tests and is listed for a device check.
edgeCases: EmojiPickerView is created once in AndroidView's factory and keeps its own state across recompositions; columns and rows are applied on update.
The latest onEmojiPicked is called, also after the lambda changes between recompositions.
Give the picker a bounded height when it sits in a scrolling column; the default 320dp does this.

parityExceptions.reason: The system EmojiPickerView applies skin tones itself on a long press, and it has no search, skin-tone button or footer preview and no emoji keyword data to search, so the web search field, the skin-tone button and the footer are not drawn; its category headings are the system's own.
parityExceptions.convention: the platform emoji picker (AndroidX EmojiPickerView) owns recents and skin tones, as the keyboard emoji panel does
